key_insight: DrivIng couples a large-scale, multimodal real-world driving dataset with a high-fidelity digital twin, enabling controlled, repeatable simulation and direct sim-to-real evaluations for perception systems.
problem_solved: Existing driving datasets lack full digital-twin fidelity, which prevents systematic edge-case generation, sensor-ablation studies, and reliable sim-to-real validation of perception algorithms.
method: Collect large-scale, synchronized multimodal data (cameras, LiDAR, radar, GPS/IMU) with rich metadata and dense annotations.
Construct a full digital twin: photorealistic scene reconstruction, dynamic actor modeling, and precise programmable sensor models for replay and perturbation.
Provide annotation/benchmark suites and tooling to run controlled experiments (edge-case injection, sensor modification, sim-to-real transfer evaluations).
impact: DrivIng lets AI/ML practitioners run reproducible, high-fidelity experiments to stress-test perception models, perform sensor- and condition-level ablations, and accelerate safe sim-to-real deployment of autonomous-driving systems.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison: real-world sensor captures vs. the digital twin photorealistic render
Multi-sensor timeline strip showing synchronized camera, LiDAR, radar, and GPS/IMU frames
Storyboard of an edge-case simulation (e.g., occlusion, heavy rain, sensor noise injection) with before/after model outputs
Benchmark chart comparing model performance across sensors and environmental conditions (day/night, weather, traffic density)
paper_title: DrivIng: A Large-Scale Multimodal Driving Dataset with Full Digital Twin Integration
paper_authors: Dominik Rößle, Xujun Xie, Adithya Mohan, Venkatesh Thirugnana Sambandham, Daniel Cremers
